correctness.rationale: The three explicit degree-two elliptic quotient maps have independent invariant differential pullbacks spanning the genus-three differential space; the Klein-four norm identity makes the isogeny 2-primary and therefore an isomorphism on p-divisible groups in every odd characteristic. Multinomial coefficient extraction independently gives the Hasse polynomials for each elliptic quotient, and the coefficient-ratio congruence (using 2n=-1 and m(m+1)=-3/16 modulo p) identifies the second with a nonzero multiple of Legendre P_m(c/2). The first is a nonzero multiple of Legendre P_n(c/2). The Legendre ODE and nonzero boundary values prove all geometric roots simple and away from c=+/-2. Thus rank and a-number addition yields the exact strata and root counts. Standalone programs verify the Hasse and full genus-three Cartier ranks for every smooth coefficient over F_p, all odd p<110, and independently verify selected gcd degrees. Finite checking is supporting evidence, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Ohashi (2021, arXiv:2112.11152) establishes elliptic quotient decomposition, conditional maximality, and finite-prime isomorphism-class tables for Howe curves; Borowka-Shatsila (2023, arXiv:2308.07038) gives characteristic-zero genus-three involution/Prym geometry. Those are acknowledged. Their inspected results do not state the joint all-odd-prime coefficient stratification and exact superspecial-Prym coefficient counts or the explicit two-Legendre-polynomial/gcd solution. The historical same-pencil p=7/11 item is a special case, not an independent new result. The classical Legendre theory itself is not claimed as original. Residual risk of equivalent unindexed literature remains.

value.rationale: A motivated natural one-parameter locus of genus-three Howe curves has its complete positive-characteristic Jacobian/elliptic/Prym p-rank and Cartier a-number geometry determined for every odd prime, including exact superspecial-Prym coefficient counts and an effective exact gcd criterion for superspecial Jacobians. Unlike a new small-prime row, this supplies one uniform structural classification; simultaneous-degeneration degrees fluctuate and are not conveyed by the motivating geometric papers. It does not claim a closed formula for d_p or a classification of isomorphism classes.
